verdicts.where: Divinity: Original Sin 2 and Magicka, where a wet target takes more from some elements, Pokemon weather boosting move types, and Noita's stains. Harm sized by depth and by water speed past the victim, and a hit held until the ground dries, are in none of them.

Fallen raised by their Shaman in Diablo II, the Darklings of Slay the Spire and the catacomb skeletons of Dark Souls for the relight; the wick multiplier is near bonuses against untouched enemies (Crowbar in Risk of Rain 2, wake-up hits in Monster Hunter). The three verbs together are its own.

Dark Souls and Elden Ring, where a weapon below its stat requirement still works at reduced effect, and attribute requirements in Diablo II. Equip-load ratios punish one mismatch; a two-way penalty between a pair of attributes is not in them.
Equip load in Dark Souls and the weight stat that resists knockback in Super Smash Bros.; pickup-radius stats in every horde game. Overload paid as a lower personal deep-water line is its own.

Space Invaders, whose whole horde steps on one shared beat, beat-locked movement in Crypt of the NecroDancer, and Zilean's Time Warp, which slows or speeds. A status that makes a crowd pulse into ranks is its own.

Blastblight in Monster Hunter (a pending burst the victim can clean off, faster in water), Tristana's Explosive Charge and Explosive Arrow stacks in Path of Exile; wet-then-punished in Magicka. A burst set off only by the victim's step onto dry ground is its own.

Down-but-not-out in Gears of War: a felled fighter on either side has a short window in which a nearby ally brings it back, and a headshot or execution skips the window. Left 4 Dead and Apex Legends revives have the same two tiers; burnt bodies in Resident Evil and divine weapons in Dark Souls are the kill that denies the rising.
verdicts.mutation: Give the smoke a direction: a plume 2 metres long that leans the way the water is running, and only a flame the plume itself touches relights the wick. Whether a snuffed thing comes back then depends on which side of the other flames it was put out, upstream or down, not on a radius and a revive timer.

verdicts.where: Hodir's Biting Cold in World of Warcraft (stacks while you stand still, moving clears them) and quicksand in Super Mario and Zelda; chill building to a freeze in Path of Exile. A slow that ends as immunity to being moved is its own.

Temporal Chains in Path of Exile (effects on the cursed expire slower), Stop in Final Fantasy, and crowd control that breaks at a damage threshold in World of Warcraft. A full stop of good and bad timers that small hits do not break is its own.

Only ships that list in naval games and ordinary directional knockback or confusion; I know no status that leans a walker's heading toward the side it was struck from and is cancelled from the other side.

Sonic's scattered rings for the player half; for the enemy half, treasure goblins shedding gold while alive in Diablo III and the Plunderblade and shiny drops of Monster Hunter. Standing still as the cure is its own.

Archero, where lifting the thumb is the attack; stopping to mine in Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor and dig spots in Hades II. Stillness spent on gathering inside the crowd, not on attacking, is its own.

Charges lost in place of life (Baldur Shell in Hollow Knight, Sonic's rings) and a planted object you stay near for a bonus (banners in Path of Exile, Ley Lines in Final Fantasy XIV). Earning a stack only by a lap out and back is its own.

Timbersaw's Timber Chain in Dota 2 and Nautilus's Dredge Line in League of Legends (an anchor thrown, the hero hauled to it, harm along the way); Dandara, who cannot walk and only leaps; moving on the beat in Crypt of the NecroDancer. A class that moves only by a fixed-rhythm automatic haul is its own.

Brutal.io and Flail Rider: a flail dragged behind the player on a tether that does nothing in a straight line and whips through a crowd on a sharp turn, harm by its speed. Hammerfight is the older game built on weapon speed alone.
verdicts.mutation: Make it a drag, not a flail: the chain lies slack and harmless along the path walked, and every few seconds it is hauled taut to a straight line, dragging every body and pickup caught in the bight to that line and harming them by the distance dragged. The player lays a loop round a crowd and the haul does the work.

verdicts.where: Facing-fired weapons in Vampire Survivors (Knife, Whip), the vision cone of Darkwood and the torch of Alan Wake, and aggro drops such as Feign Death in World of Warcraft with the last-known-position search of stealth games. One shutter trading all offence for being lost is its own.

Weaver's Shukuchi in Dota 2 (unseen, harming each enemy passed through), Rek'Sai's burrow, the burrow-moving Roach of StarCraft II, and Sonic's air countdown. Air halved by depth and a hidden walk steered by a second current are its own.

Marauder sentries in Diablo III and spell totems in Path of Exile, which cast the hero's own skills, and captured map turrets; the light havens of Alan Wake. Fixed lamps on a timer the crowd wears down, kept alive by walking a round, are its own.
Bonus-experience and gold zones on arena floors, and the shoreline where shells wash up in Animal Crossing and Stardew Valley. A thin strip redrawn by each tide is its own.

Prestige in idle games (ascension in Cookie Clicker: melt the run for a permanent multiplier), stack items made permanent at full count (Tear of the Goddess into Seraph's Embrace), bank-or-ride combos in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater. Banking that leaves the banker bare is its own.

Dome Keeper, where the haul trails behind on tethers and slows you until delivered; bounty skulls carried to a turn-in in Sea of Thieves; the idol in Spelunky. Kills that are weapon, burden and pay at once are its own.

Totem play in Path of Exile: a planted object with its own life casts your skills while Decoy Totem holds the monsters and you gather. The Engineer's sentry in Team Fortress 2 and sentries in Diablo III are the same seat.
verdicts.mutation: Let the false light wreck and not fight: the lantern casts nothing, and bodies steering for it walk a straight line, cannot turn aside and gain speed all the way. They are harmed by what they run onto (pillars, hulks, deep water, each other at the lamp) in proportion to that speed, so the skill is choosing a spot with rocks between.

verdicts.where: Egocentrism in Risk of Rain 2 (every 60 seconds one of your other items is eaten and the stack grows) and Madness and Ceremonial Dagger in Balatro (each blind a Joker is destroyed and the multiplier rises). Deck-thinning and Banish are the milder forms.
verdicts.mutation: Give the dying light's strength to one heir, not 12% to all: the player names which burning light inherits the whole of what the darkened one did. The vigil becomes a line of succession ending in one overgrown flame, and the hidden candle comes back to inherit from it.

verdicts.where: The water shield of Sonic 3 and Noita's Freeze Field and circle fields, a carried bubble that changes what liquid does; Cloud Nine in Pokemon cancelling weather for all. A bubble sized by the depth stood in, which bursts brine on those who enter, is its own.

The ninja rope of Worms, which wraps round terrain, the flat swing round a post in Sling Drift, and Snake Pass coiling a pole for grip. A wrap that turns movement into being immovable and returns pushes is its own.

Surfaces in Divinity: Original Sin, where fire dries a water tile and the status rules change with it; stand-still zones like Bustling Fungus in Risk of Rain 2. A harmless patch placed by choosing where to stop is its own.

The ranger's favoured enemy in Dungeons and Dragons and Hunter's Mark in World of Warcraft; bonuses against a monster family in Diablo. A mark taken by the strike, always the nearest body, overwritten every cast, is its own.

Whirlwind and tornado towers in Bloons TD that blow the line back the way it came, fear effects that turn enemies round, and knock-into-others harm from Poseidon in Hades. An eddy born only by brushing an obstacle is its own.

Tether lines that harm what crosses them: the Electropylon Driver of Returnal, Loader's pylon in Risk of Rain 2, beams strung between two ships in cooperative shooters. A far end adrift on the tide is its own; the harm-by-speed rule is the flail's, as in water-15.

Qix, Volfied and Paper.io, where closing your own line is the attack, the capture loops of Pokemon Ranger, and Snake, where crossing yourself is the event. Striking along the groove, not inside a loop, is its own.

Pull skills and push skills everywhere; vacuums that take the small and leave the heavy (Luigi's Mansion, the Suck Cannon of Ratchet and Clank); spells with opposite effects by type, as healing harms the undead. One cast that sends the swarm out and drags the heavy in is its own.
Ignite in Path of Exile, built from the single strongest hit; Zed's Death Mark in League of Legends and Bide in Pokemon, which store damage and replay it. A per-toll record replayed whole is its own.

The minecarts of the Dairy Plant in Vampire Survivors (touch one and it runs through the crowd), the football of Survivor.io, and props kicked into enemies in Half-Life 2 and Dark Messiah. One lasting piece of drift the player shoulders about is its own.
Water finding its level in Noita, floodgates in Dwarf Fortress and From Dust, and the wave pushes of Hades. As a skill aimed by the ground that leaves both depths changed, I know no match.

Charges built by standing still (Brotato, Halls of Torment) and gauges filled by pressure taken (Galio's Shield of Durand in League of Legends, the V-Gauge of Street Fighter V). A charge that is the crowd's own lean, aimed by its densest side, is its own.

Graze in Touhou and the Buzz system of Psyvariar, the speed bonus on blows in Mount and Blade, and the Garlic aura of Vampire Survivors. A near miss that is the attack itself, sized by closing speed, is its own.
Pinball bumpers, which answer every knock, thorns and retaliation totems, and drifting sea mines. An emitter rung by crowding and carried by the tide is its own.

Culling Strike in Path of Exile and the Old Guillotine of Risk of Rain 2; deaths that set nothing off, as exile in Magic: The Gathering, Silence and transform in Hearthstone, 'Slain Monsters Rest in Peace' in Diablo II and frozen exploders in Deep Rock Galactic. The pairing, aimed at death effects, is its own.

The Engineer's pressure mines in Risk of Rain 2, which arm up to full strength over time, Zyra's seeds in League of Legends, woken by coming back with a spell, and the Demoman's stickies. Mines set off only by the player's return and eaten by the crowd are its own.
Terrains and weather in Pokemon that boost a move only on the right ground, Spell Echo and while-stationary supports in Path of Exile. A repeat that belongs to still water is its own.

Convention of Elements in Diablo III, a bonus on a fixed repeating clock that players learn and fight around; the Balance Druid's Eclipse in World of Warcraft and turn-count relics in Slay the Spire are the same learnable cycle.
verdicts.mutation: Count the extra casts from the speed of the water at the character's feet, not from the clock: none in slack water, one in a stream, two in a race. Mid-tide is still the strong time, but arches, channels and eddies let the player find fast or slack water at any moment, so it is a rule about where to stand as well as when.

verdicts.where: Remote mines in Path of Exile and the Demoman's stickies in Team Fortress 2: casts stored where they would land and all let go together later, for more. Released by the clock and not the player it is the time bomb: Future Sight in Pokemon, Delayed Blast Fireball in Dungeons and Dragons.
verdicts.mutation: Sink each cast where the character stands and let the buoys drift on the current until the toll, releasing wherever the tide has carried them and stronger for every metre travelled. The player sows casts upstream of where the crowd will be at the bell and has to read the stream, which no mine or time bomb asks.

verdicts.where: The Geomancer of Final Fantasy Tactics and Final Fantasy V, whose one command gives a different attack and rider by the terrain underfoot, and Secret Power and Nature Power in Pokemon, whose effect is read from the ground of the battle.
verdicts.mutation: Have the skill carry the ground with it and not just read it: it takes a sample from under the character at the cast and lays a 3-second patch of that ground under its victims, deep water on dry stone, a dry pan in the shallows, silt in a clear channel. The rider is terrain moved from one place to another, which sets off the wet and dry rules there.

verdicts.where: Sonic's rings scattered to be gathered again, the dropped gold bags of Shovel Knight, and guns that fire your own money (the Microtransaction Gun in Enter the Gungeon). A per-cast cost dropped behind into the pursuit is its own.

The Knife and Whip of Vampire Survivors, which fire only the way you face, and narrowing supports in Path of Exile; it also repeats the cone of water-16. As a socket on any automatic skill it is its own.

Bonuses against untouched enemies (Crowbar in Risk of Rain 2, Ambush in Diablo III) and per-target lockouts (Braum's stun immunity in League of Legends, diminishing returns in World of Warcraft). A triple bite paid for with immunity until the toll is its own.

Ley Lines in Final Fantasy XIV, a placed zone you must stand in to cast better, reserved auras in Path of Exile, and lanes in arena battle games. A bonus that exists only on a bearing between two landmarks is its own.

Water streams carrying drops to one collection point in Minecraft farms, experience gems merging in Vampire Survivors, and Brotato doubling what was left on the ground. Loot sent away to the lee of pillars at a premium is its own.
Link Skills in MapleStory and soldier bonds in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen, where a bondmate's death hurts the survivor. A gift paid from the holder's pool that turns to a debt on death is its own.

Shroud in Magic: The Gathering (cannot be targeted by anyone, your own spells included), spell immunity in Dota 2 that also refused allied spells, and the Warforged of Dungeons and Dragons, immune to much and healed by half. Path of Exile keystones are built this way: an immunity paired with the loss of its matching benefit.
verdicts.mutation: Make the wrap seal in whatever is on the character when it is wound: switching it on stops every wet condition already on them from acting or expiring, and switching it off lets them all resume. It becomes a way to carry Brine sealed across dry ground to a font, at the price of the pool and the heavier blows.

verdicts.where: Pokemon: Burmy's cloak, set by the ground of its last battle, and Eevee or Magneton evolving into different forms by where they stand when they level up. Stat growth in Final Fantasy Tactics, decided by the job held at the moment of the level, is the same rule.
verdicts.mutation: Pour it hot and let it set over the next 10 seconds: the share of that time spent in current, still water and deep water becomes the share of reach, area and harm in the finished shape, and every second on dry ground is wax lost. The pick is a short run the player makes through the water, with a blended result no menu or map spot would give.

verdicts.where: Moving objective zones (Crazy King in Halo, Hardpoint in Call of Duty) and shoreline spawns in Animal Crossing; it also repeats water-19. A bonus band that walks the map with the tide is its own.
Near-miss and oncoming boosts in Burnout, named gaps in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater, slalom gates. Stacks earned by threading narrow places with the crowd at the shoulder are its own.

Chaos boons in Hades (pay now, blessing after a set number of chambers), the Invisible Joker and interest in Balatro, saving for interest in Teamfight Tactics. Loading one known toll with several nails is its own.
N'loth in Slay the Spire (give up a relic for better offers from then on), devil deals in The Binding of Isaac, altars in Spelunky. The price being the best unbanked find is its own.

Rain Dance and Sunny Day in Pokemon (spend the turn to set the field for five turns), the Rod of Seasons and the Sun's Song in Zelda. Taken mid-run in place of an upgrade to hold the tide, it is its own.
Opt-in risk for the next reward (Shrine of the Mountain in Risk of Rain 2, flawless doors in Dead Cells) and buffs renewed each wave. One wade per tide worn as a line is its own.

Jellyfish that float slowly at the player in Risk of Rain 2, the wind-driven Angry Tumbler of Terraria, logs and hazards on river currents in Frogger. A horde whose only legs are a readable tide is its own.

Fire Keese in Zelda, which relight at any flame, Fallen revived by a Shaman in Diablo II, Crimson Heads in Resident Evil, Darklings in Slay the Spire. An enemy dying on its own clock and worth more left unlit is its own.

Armour that softens only on the right ground (Agnaktor and Lavasioth in Monster Hunter), enemies harmed by water in Minecraft, shield bubbles that must be entered in Path of Exile. A shield ended by depth the player would rather avoid is its own.
Zerg on and off creep in StarCraft, sharks and crocodiles that are deadly in water and helpless ashore (Maneater, Far Cry), ramming chargers. Speed and harm both read from the surface is its own.

Raid debuffs cleansed only at a marked pool (World of Warcraft, Final Fantasy XIV) and wet-then-punished in Magicka and Divinity: Original Sin. It is water-06 on an enemy; safe ground made the thing that hurts is its own.

Sleepers laid over the loot: draugr in the barrows of Skyrim, Decayed Guardians in Breath of the Wild, Armos statues, sleeper zombies in 7 Days to Die, the Witch in Left 4 Dead. The wake-all on a clock is nightfall in Dying Light and Minecraft.
verdicts.mutation: Tie the waking to the taking, not to nearness: the mounds never stir at ebb, but each find lifted from the foreshore unbeds the nearest mound, which rises only when the returning water covers it. The flood then brings exactly as many heavy dead as the player took finds, from the places they were taken.

verdicts.where: Burrowers with a surface tell (Molduga in Breath of the Wild, the fin and barrels of Jaws games) and river Zoras that surface to strike. A float the player can cut to blind it is its own.

The mimic chest of Dark Souls, with its honest tell (the chain) and its reward for dealing with it from a distance, crossed with the will-o'-the-wisp that leads to an ambush (Dungeons and Dragons, The Witcher 3) and the anglerfish lure; From Software's glowing item with enemies lying round it.
verdicts.mutation: Drop the ambush and make it a thief of the moment: a Jibber lights only in the last 15 seconds before a toll, within 20 metres of the gate about to open, and has nothing hidden round it. Its whole harm is that the player is standing at the wrong lamp when the bell sounds and owes another tide; the missing reflection and the bob stay as the tells.

verdicts.where: Water-funnel mob grinders in Minecraft, which also gather the drops, one-way conveyors into crushers in Mario, pinball outlanes. A trap that is the district's loot collector and opens at slack water is its own.

Stage hazards that carry fighters off in Super Smash Bros. (Spirit Train, Big Blue), minecarts in Vampire Survivors, conveyor tiles in Bomberman. A sweep that moves crowd, loot and player to one known heap is its own.

Bone-throwing skeletons in Castlevania, which spend themselves, crippled limbs in Fallout (leg for speed, head for sight), and the Like-Like of Zelda, which takes one named thing. The raised shape naming the faculty at stake is its own.

Clock-sector sweeps in Final Fantasy XIV and World of Warcraft raids, the Lost Sinner's dark arena in Dark Souls II, which the player can light, torch-relighting bosses in Zelda, shrinking arenas. Winning sectors back through the smoke and a last phase dodged by ear are its own.

Sectioned armour in MechWarrior and BattleTech, where the damaged side is turned away from you, and wounds and tenderised parts in Monster Hunter. Sculpting the flaw in one phase and having the next cast from it is its own.

Leviathan in Final Fantasy XIV (water surging across the deck) and the raid habit of hiding behind a pillar from a room-wide blast; rising-water arenas in Zelda and Mario. Water level as the phase counter and the boss's own lee as the shelter are its own.

Mordekaiser's Realm of Death in League of Legends and the brain room of Yogg-Saron in World of Warcraft: taken into a sealed space on a hard clock, the only place the boss can be hurt. A clock that is a flame the player may put out is its own.
Tide levels in Salmon Run (Splatoon), the tides of Mario Kart beach tracks, tilting stages in Super Smash Bros. A standing wave with a level, fast middle is its own.
One-way doors and conveyors on timers in Bomberman and Zelda dungeons, rapids chutes in Donkey Kong Country. Chokepoints that run one way for a tide and then turn round are its own.
Low tide in Salmon Run opening the foreshore, Levolution in Battlefield 4, day and night map states. Hulks that float and ground somewhere new each flood are its own.
Convention of Elements in Diablo III (a bonus that rotates on a clock) and the fixed cast order of a wand in Noita. Scheduling which ordinary node is tripled at which toll is its own.

Free respecs in Diablo III against permanent exclusive picks (Ascendancy in Path of Exile, policy trees in Civilization V). Trial at half strength and a commitment that closes the rest of a cluster are its own.

Only redstone signal strength in Minecraft (falling one per block until a repeater restores it) and supply-range falloff in strategy games; I know no character tree that weakens nodes by path length or pays for closing a loop.

Night Stalker in Dota 2, formidable for one half of the clock and plain for the other, and the Sun Stone, Moon Stone and Celestial Stone of Terraria (works by day, by night, always); Solar and Lunar Eclipse for the Druid in World of Warcraft.
verdicts.mutation: Let the ground, not the clock, decide which bank is live: flood-bank nodes work while the character stands in water and ebb-bank nodes while on dry ground. The tide then sets how much of each ground a district offers at that toll, and the player chooses a build by where the thumb goes.

verdicts.where: Adding and removing random affixes in Path of Exile, and the sealed affix of Last Epoch, set aside under the working ones. A strict last-on, first-off stack with a buried history is its own.

The Item World of Disgaea (an item grows by how deep you dive and get out), legendary gems ranked by Greater Rift depth in Diablo III, weapons that grow and can be lost in Dark Cloud. A record of depth as the only grade is its own.

Weapon affinities in Vagrant Story, shaped by what the weapon is used on, challenge perks in Fallout: New Vegas, growth by use in The Elder Scrolls. A line written by the deed you led in against your own average is its own.

Unidentified items in Diablo and NetHack (wearable unread in NetHack), unidentified sets paying double in the chaos recipe of Path of Exile, sealed crates worth more unopened. A sealed state that is a usable item, and a gamble the player may decline, is its own.

Tidal Wave from Leviathan in Final Fantasy XIV and raid blasts dodged behind a pillar in World of Warcraft; screen-crossing hazard waves. A wave that carries loot and horde too, with whelps and a reversed stream after, is its own.

Stand-in-the-circle objectives (the teleporter in Risk of Rain 2, events in Diablo IV), Tail Tag in Fall Guys (hold it at the final instant), musical chairs. Presence staked by the second on an uncertain instant is its own.

ZombiU and bones files in NetHack, where a later character recovers the dead one's goods at the death spot; corpse runs in Dark Souls; stand-and-defend recoveries like the Black Box in Deep Rock Galactic. A 75-second defence of a flame is its own.

The destroyer that breaks loose and grounds on the island in Paracel Storm (Battlefield 4), moving-platform refuges, stage hazards that plough through fighters. A hull that regrounds as a new wall each flood is its own.

The Rain spell of Divinity: Original Sin (douses fire, wets everyone, primes other statuses), storms in Breath of the Wild, rain in Pokemon. Player and horde put on one pulse is its own, by way of water-05.

Fog and storm events that cut sight for a while: roaming fog banks in Sea of Thieves, storm bursts in Hard Rain (Left 4 Dead 2), fog rounds in Hunt: Showdown, darkness in the Delve of Path of Exile and in Darkest Dungeon.
verdicts.mutation: Let the fog lie low on the water and hide the ground while every flame shows through it at full distance: in the bank the player sees lamps, lit bodies, votives and their own light, but not water depth, pickups, stubs or anything unlit. Finding the way is done by lights alone, which is exactly when a false one matters.

verdicts.where: Rogue Legacy: Charon takes whatever gold is left at the gate, so runs are never summed and an upgrade must be afforded by one run alone. Cells handed in or lost between levels in Dead Cells follow the same rule.
verdicts.mutation: Let layers join or part by how the vigil ended: a vigil banked alive may be merged with the bed beneath it into one thicker bed, while a fatal one sets as a hard crust that no node can root through. A node needs one unbroken bed as deep as its cost, so the unit of saving is the run of survivals between two deaths.

verdicts.where: Legacies in Sunless Sea (the dead captain passes on one distinctive thing), relics of dead heroes in Massive Chalice, the lineage of Rogue Legacy. A working tree node shaped by how the dead differed from the rest is its own.

Shortcuts in Spelunky and Greater Rift level select in Diablo III (start deeper, up to your record), and heat bounties in Hades, which pay only for a new best. Skipped levels still chosen in a row is its own.

Salmon Run in Splatoon, where each wave has its own tide level, tide levels in Donkey Kong Country and New Super Mario Bros., seasons in Don't Starve. A tide that moves through each interval on a readable curve, with slack and springs, is its own.

Loop Hero: the campfire tile is the one place to retreat with everything, reached once per loop at the moment the loop counter and the danger step up. Timed exits in Escape from Tarkov and the portals of Dark and Darker are the window alone.
verdicts.mutation: Give the lock a capacity set by the tide in place of a yes or no: each slack it banks finds up to that toll's range, two at a neap and six at a spring, and the character goes through only with the last of them. A hoard has to be sent out over several tolls or saved for a spring, and what to send first is the question.

verdicts.where: Chaos boons and curses in Hades that last a set number of chambers, the oldest item falling off the inventory in Loop Hero, set rotation in Hearthstone. Every upgrade expiring on one clock in the order taken is its own.

Buried stashes in DayZ and Rust: goods hidden on purpose in the hostile map, kept through your death and dug up by your next character. Storehouses in Shiren the Wanderer and buried treasure in Sea of Thieves are the same cache.
verdicts.mutation: Let the water work on what is sunk: for each vigil a find lies under its buoy it takes one crust, a property of that district's kind laid over its own, and after three it can be hauled only at a spring ebb. The buoy is a slow workshop in hostile ground as well as a bequest, and leaving a thing down longer is a real choice.

verdicts.where: Legacy in Wildermyth (heroes of a finished campaign join a lasting roster, keeping some things and losing others) and league characters passing one way into Standard in Path of Exile and Last Epoch.
verdicts.mutation: Make the casting reproduce the run's marks, as lost-wax does: each district cleared without a heavy blow casts clean, fixing one node of the path at full strength for good, and each district survived at under a fifth of life casts a flaw, a named weakness to that district's water. The player pours how they played and may refuse a flawed casting.

verdicts.where: Death Stranding, where cargo weight meets river currents and a dropped load drifts downstream to be chased, the idol of Spelunky as treasure and thrown weapon, carry weight in extraction games. Weight as steadiness against the water is its own.

The torch in Darkest Dungeon (dimmer is richer and riskier), Light Radius in Diablo, boons with a curse from Chaos in Hades. Every upgrade offered at the same two prices, one of them sight, is its own.

Compartments in Barotrauma and FTL, where doors hold water or air between rooms and opening one equalises them; the Water Temple in Zelda; room-lock doors in The Binding of Isaac. A tide that works every door by one rule is its own.
Super Smash Bros., where the more hurt a fighter is the farther it is thrown, and low-life bonuses in Path of Exile. Missing life changing how the water treats the body is its own.
